text:
ben (kvcache): heads up — saw repeated 150–300ms tail spikes on a couple of production nodes during KV cache refills this morning. correlates with bursts of small requests + one large background eviction. nsys shows big gaps where kernels stop and host-side calls appear. link: https://perf.example/trace/1877654321 :thinking_face:

maya (perf): can you paste the nsys command & a tiny slice? that helps me see the stack (host vs device).

ben (kvcache): here's the exact capture i grabbed (shortened):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,cudnn --output=alloc-burst --capture-range=nvtx
# slice: 00:00:12.300 - 00:00:12.950
# timeline: lots of small kernels, then a 220ms gap labeled Host:cudaMalloc
```
there's an NVTX range "kv_refill" that encloses the gap. also see repeated hostalloc events in perfetto.

sam (runtime): probability that suballocator is handing off to cudaMalloc when a per-thread slab runs dry. if the handoff path is synchronous we take the allocator lock and block other threads. did you see global lock contention in the trace?

ben (kvcache): yep — stack shows allocator mutex held around the host call. spikes line up with when many requests touch new model prefixes and cause lots of small allocations + a few >1MB allocations that bypass the suballoc path.

maya (perf): two quick experiments to triage: 1) increase suballoc_max_bytes to reduce bypass, 2) enable async-warmup (background allocation thread) so cudaMalloc doesn't run on the hot path. small commands:
```
# runtime flags
--suballoc_max_bytes=2097152  # 2MB
--subpools_per_worker=4
--enable_async_warmup=true
```
run both for ~5m under similar QPS and compare p95/p99.

elaine (infra): i'll spin a perfetto with heap and mmap events on one repro node so we can see page allocs + host latency. attaching template:
```
perfetto --out=trace.pftrace -c - <<EOF
buffers: { size_kb: 10240 }
data_sources { config { name: "linux.heapprofd" } }
EOF
```
will post when done.

alloc-bot: AllocationMonitor detected 7 cudaMalloc > 100ms in 10m window on node runtime-12, correlated with NVTX tag "kv_refill". Alert: low "free-suballocs" in pool 3.

ben (kvcache): quick results — bumped suballoc_max to 2MB + subpools=4: p99 tail dropped ~38% across the sampled nodes. however fragmentation metric (free-run-chunks) increased slowly after ~1h, and we got a couple of 80ms hostallocs still for long-sequence batches. so it helps but doesn't fully eliminate spikes.

sam (runtime): expected tradeoff. next steps: 1) implement background warmup to pre-allocate larger subpools during low load, 2) add non-blocking fallback (queue request that waits on async host alloc rather than holding global lock). i'll prototype the warmup patch.

maya (perf): i'll run a focused perfetto + flamegraph on the patched suballocator branch. also want to check kernel selection latency is unchanged (we should avoid moving stalls into kernel-launch delays).

elaine (infra): perfetto uploaded: https://perf.example/trace/1877654400 — shows page faults and mmap churn before the big host stalls; suggests host-side fragmentation + OS-level delays also play a role.

ben (kvcache): going to add a telemetry gauge for "suballoc_free_bytes" and a short-running synthetic that hits small prefixes to reproduce locally. will post a short trace when done. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam (runtime): plan: prototype warmup + non-blocking fallback this week, bench on canary, roll to the cluster if p99 improves and fragmentation stays within thresholds. assigning: sam -> warmup patch, maya -> perf runs, ben -> telemetry + repro.

maya (perf): note — when comparing traces, filter NVTX range names and align by request id. small Q: do we have deterministic request IDs for the repro harness? if not i can add them.

ben (kvcache): i do, will add them to the harness and push a repro branch shortly.

alloc-bot: Follow-up: created ticket RINF-2374 "suballocator warmup + non-blocking hostalloc fallback" and added initial repro links.

sam (runtime): good. closing the loop after the canary run. :rocket:
